identity.title: Genome-wide identification of the EIN3/EIL gene family in potato and characterization of StEIN3/EIL2 in response to phosphorus starvation.

content.abstract: Phosphorus (P) is an essential macronutrient, and low inorganic phosphate (Pi) availability is a major constraint on potato (Solanum tuberosum) production. The ETHYLENE-INSENSITIVE3/EIN3-LIKE (EIN3/EIL) transcription factors integrate ethylene signaling with Pi starvation (low Pi) responses in model species, but this family has not been systematically characterized in potato. Here, nine StEIN3/EIL genes were identified in the potato genome; they are distributed unevenly across five chromosomes and appear to have expanded through tandem and segmental duplication. All members are intron-less and retain the conserved N-terminal EIN3 DNA-binding domain. Transcriptomic profiling and RT-qPCR analyses revealed divergent tissue-specific expression patterns, among which StEIN3/EIL2 was strongly and rapidly induced in roots by Pi deprivation and, together with StEIN3/EIL4 and StEIN3/EIL8, localized to the nucleus. CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of StEIN3/EIL2 compromised root growth and reduced soluble Pi accumulation specifically under low Pi, identifying StEIN3/EIL2 as a positive regulator of the Pi starvation response. StEIN3/EIL2 interacted with the promoter of the central Pi signaling regulator StPHR1 in a yeast one-hybrid assay and activated transcription from this promoter in a heterologous transient system, and knockout of StPHR1 abolished low Pi-induced root elongation and reduced Pi accumulation. These findings establish a StEIN3/EIL2-StPHR1 module that links ethylene signaling to Pi starvation adaptation in potato and provide candidate targets for breeding Pi-efficient cultivars.
